card.title: RAAF WALRUS
card.text:
Deployment: Forecast. 
Becomes Veteran at the end of turn.
card.flavorText: The RAAF Walrus, originally called the Supermarine Seagull V, was a ship-based amphibious aircraft designed to meet an Australian requirement. The RAAF ordered 24 aircraft in 1933, for use as spotter and reconnaissance aircraft aboard Royal Australian Navy cruisers. Deliveries began in 1935, with most aircraft first sent to Point Cook for seaplane crew training. The type later served from HMAS Australia, Canberra, Sydney, Perth, and Hobart. In Australian service, the aircraft was launched by catapult, landed on the sea, and was lifted back aboard by crane. It was used for patrols, scouting, gunnery support, and general naval duties. In August 1940, a Walrus from HMAS Hobart attacked Italian headquarters at Zeila in British Somaliland with bombs and machine guns. The RAAF also used the type with No. 5 Squadron, No. 9 Squadron, No. 11 Squadron, and No. 101 Flight. The Royal New Zealand Navy also used Walruses aboard HMNZS Achilles and HMNZS Leander, while the RNZAF operated the type with No. 5 Squadron and its Seaplane Training Flight.
